clue.text: This BBC centre agreed (in other words) to make a programme

definitions.text: This BBC centre agreed (in other words) to make a programme

parts.words: This BBC centre agreed (in other words) to make a programme
parts.note: the BBC studio in Birmingham, plus another phrase meaning agreed (at one), names a lunchtime television show

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's regional studio consents to produce a new show.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the BBC's old Birmingham studio; 'agreed (in other words)' means put 'at one' after it, giving the daytime show Pebble Mill at One.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birmingham broadcasting studio gave its name to a long-running daytime magazine show.

clue.text: Tidy up pages, including margin

indicators.note: including means the pages hold the margin inside them

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so PP for pages
a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: Neatening the pages, margins and all.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to make oneself neat and smart.

clue.text: Having imprisoned .Kate, worker died under a curse

indicators.note: having imprisoned means the bee holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a worker bee
Kate is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A labourer locked up Kate and then died cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Shakespeare's shrew. 'Beshrew' is an old word for curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To beshrew is an archaic way to wish evil on someone, so beshrewed means cursed.

clue.text: Estate first to provide sportsground — divine!

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground
divine means spiritual

explanation.surface: An estate given over to a sports field is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is London's famous cricket ground. The bishops in the House of Lords were the first of the three estates of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishops sitting in the upper House traditionally formed the first estate of the realm.

clue.text: It's' stupid to have no micro-development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of no micro evolve into a new form

explanation.surface: It would be foolish to refuse to develop microcomputers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' rearranges NO MICRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Moronic means foolish or idiotic.

clue.text: Appreciates appearance in the saddle

parts.note: looks means appearance
a rider in the saddle is up

explanation.surface: Someone admires how a rider looks on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appreciates' looks like admires; here it means rises in value, as a share price improves.
explanation.definitionFit: When a market looks up it improves, just as a share appreciates in value.

clue.text: Architect had a horsy mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of a horse or other animal

explanation.surface: An architect whose mother was rather equine in looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect. 'Horsy mother' is a breeder's word for a mare that has foaled.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam was a celebrated Scottish neoclassical designer of buildings.

clue.text: What finally would be beyond Wilde's means

definitions.text: What finally would be beyond Wilde's means

parts.words: What finally would be beyond Wilde's means
parts.note: Oscar Wilde's deathbed quip that he was expiring beyond his means

explanation.surface: Something Oscar Wilde could not afford in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde reputedly said near the end, 'I am dying beyond my means'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde joked that his final days in Paris were spent expiring beyond his means.

clue.text: Island refugee whose master sounded so exultant

definitions.text: Island refugee whose master sounded so exultant

parts.words: Island refugee whose master sounded so exultant
parts.note: the castaway's companion, whose master's name is said like 'crow so', crowing being exulting

explanation.surface: A fugitive on an island whose employer sounded triumphant.
explanation.walkthrough: Crusoe sounds like 'crow so', and to crow is to exult; Defoe's castaway named his companion after the day they met.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's castaway rescued a native and named him after the weekday they met.

clue.text: IRA formation determined to create so comfortable a breathing-space

indicators.note: formation means the letters of IRA are formed anew

parts.note: conditioned means determined, governed by circumstances

explanation.surface: A paramilitary group resolved to set up a cosy hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formation' rearranges IRA. The definition describes a room cooled and freshened by a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with cooled, filtered ventilation is pleasant to breathe in.

clue.text: He accepts risks in certain races initially

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word races only

explanation.surface: A gambler who takes chances on certain races.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter takes on other people's risks in exchange for premiums.

clue.text: Belief in Number One returning after work at home

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the work and home pieces

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
in means at home

indicators.note: returning means the two pieces from Number One are read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Faith in the boss coming back after working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Number One read backwards sits after the work and home pieces; 'at home' is IN as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or conviction someone holds.

clue.text: Painful experiences about new, sort of choral works

indicators.note: about means the pangs piece goes around the other letters

parts.note: pangs are sudden sharp pains

indicators.note: new means the letters of sort are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Agonies over a new kind of piece for the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' here is the anagram signal for sort, and 'about' has the painful experiences surrounding the result; 'sort of' looks like a hedge but 'of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Part-songs are pieces for several voices, usually unaccompanied, sung in harmony.

clue.text: In Havana wild garlic has no end of a smell

indicators.note: wild signals the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
has no means a letter is removed from the garlic
end of picks the closing letter of smell

explanation.surface: In Cuba, wild garlic has lost its pungency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' a smell is L; 'has no' takes it out of GARLIC, leaving GARIC, which 'wild' rearranges. 'In Havana' looks like a place; Havana is the definition, a Cuban smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A Havana is a cigar made in Cuba.

clue.text: Finalize most 'of the points raised

parts.note: three of the four compass points, south, east and west
raised means up

explanation.surface: Settling most of the matters that were brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sew up a deal is to settle or conclude it.

clue.text: Part of the service where dressing for dinner is retained

definitions.text: Part of the service where dressing for dinner is retained

parts.words: Part of the service where dressing for dinner is retained
parts.note: a dinner-service vessel holding gravy, the dressing for a meal

explanation.surface: Part of a church service where formal evening wear is kept on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church service or the navy; it is a dinner service, and 'dressing' is sauce, not clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat-shaped jug holds gravy at table as part of a set of dinner crockery.

clue.text: How one might plead to get Community farm policy under control

parts.note: CAP is the European Community's Common Agricultural Policy
in hand means under control

explanation.surface: How farmers might beg to get Brussels' agricultural policy tamed.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming humbly asking for something, as a beggar holds out a hat.

clue.text: Constituents make pact plain to candidate

indicators.note: constituents means the component letters of pact plain are assembled into a new word

explanation.surface: Voters make a clear deal with the person standing for election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' (in the sense of components) rearranges PACT PLAIN; the surface wants it to mean voters.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is someone putting themselves forward for a job or post.

clue.text: Rare foreign articles finished

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite one
finished means done

explanation.surface: Unusual imported items, all sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' looks like scarce; here it is meat lightly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare steak is cooked only briefly, so not fully done.

clue.text: Dispatch, box, available. to. a party in office?

definitions.text: Dispatch, box, available. to. a party in office?

parts.words: Dispatch, box, available. to. a party in office?
parts.note: a tray for letters going out, read as the Commons dispatch box used by the governing party

explanation.surface: The Commons dispatch box belongs to whichever party is in government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dispatch Box is where ministers speak in the Commons; here it is an office tray for outgoing mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing letters waiting to be sent are placed in a desk tray for dispatch.

clue.text: Keats's comforting description of 7

parts.note: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale is 'half in love with' a soothing death

explanation.surface: A Romantic poet's soothing account of passing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is DYING. Keats wrote in Ode to a Nightingale 'I have been half in love with easeful Death'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats used the word for soothing, restful death in his nightingale ode.

clue.text: Mean to be just, were we to add a quarter in advance

indicators.note: were we to add means the answer becomes the other word once a letter is supplied, so remove that letter
in advance places the extra quarter at the front of the word

parts.note: just means simply
S, south, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Being fair to all would mean adding a quarter up front.
explanation.walkthrough: Put S (a compass quarter) in front of the answer and it becomes SIMPLY, 'just'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to suggest or signify it without saying it outright.

clue.text: French material rejected by this poet

indicators.note: rejected means the fabric word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: toile is a French linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A poet who turned down some French fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns TOILE back to front. T.S. Eliot is the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: T.S. Eliot was a major modernist writer of verse.

clue.text: Batting record Times leader describes as fatuous

parts.note: a batsman batting is in
EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial dismisses a batting record as silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' suggests an editorial; it is just the T of Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or foolishly lacking in skill.

clue.text: Declared for trial if that's the Board's conclusion

parts.note: a test is a trial
i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: conclusion picks the closing letter of the word Board's

explanation.surface: Gave evidence in court, assuming the board decides it that way.
explanation.walkthrough: IE (that is) supplies 'that's'; the last letter of Board's is S.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to state something solemnly, especially in court.

clue.text: Topless kind of theatre in the park

definitions.text: kind of theatre in the park
definitions.meaning: a type of outdoor stage, as in London's Regent's Park

explanation.walkthrough: London's Regent's Park has a famous outdoor theatre. 'Topless' suggests nudity but means roofless.

clue.text: Sweet, tender and a model of industry

parts.note: tender means fond, affectionate
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: A sweet, gentle person who is also a model worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste used for confectionery and icing.

clue.text: Better system for child-bearing

definitions.meaning: a better is one who bets; the totalisator is a betting system
carrying, as one might carry a child about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who places bets, not 'more good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator pools wagers on races, and to tote is to carry.

clue.text: Hit song Chevalier didn't want to swop

definitions.text: Hit song Chevalier didn't want to swop

parts.words: Hit song Chevalier didn't want to swop
parts.note: a music-hall song by Albert Chevalier about a wife he would not exchange for anything

explanation.surface: A music-hall favourite about a partner the singer would never trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Chevalier, a Victorian music-hall star, sang of his wife; Dutch is Cockney slang for wife, and he says he would not swap her.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's title is Cockney for 'my wife', whom the singer would never exchange.
